name: Documentation command reference
description: Searchable command reference: Filter by group to search for commands, purposes, and parameters and highlight matches; expand a command to view descriptions, parameter tables, and reproducible examples.
scenarios: List keyboard shortcuts, scripts, or configuration commands
Find in long command lists by purpose and parameters

boundaries: List of commands, shortcuts, or scripts for use in ShowAI documentation: One line per command plus a sentence of purpose that expands descriptions, parameters, and examples.
Suitable for 10–150 items; not used for data tables that require sorting or multi-column numerical comparisons.
Read-only display: Search, filter and expand only change the local view and do not modify the page data.

usage.purpose: Allow readers to find commands by task: enter keywords or parameter names to immediately narrow the scope, and expand and directly copy the example.
structure: Top search box: matches commands, purposes, and parameters (parameter names and descriptions) at the same time; multiple keywords are separated by spaces and all must be matched; matching text is highlighted. Esc to clear, ↓ to enter the list.
Group filtering: "All" and each group, the number is the number of matches under the current search; click the selected group again to return to "All".

The list is divided into groups: each line is a command in monospaced font (program name is faded, subcommands are bolded, placeholders are faded) and a sentence of purpose; only commands with matching parameters will list the matching parameters.
Expand a row to show detail, parameter table, and example with copy button. Commands without detail, flags, and example cannot be expanded.
If there is no match, an empty status is displayed. You can clear the search or return to all groups.

inputs.meaning: Group, in order of presentation; groups 3–7 recommended.
Group ID, referenced by commands[].group, unique.
Group name, displayed on filter buttons and section titles.
Commands are arranged in the order of display; commands in the same group are displayed in the original order under this group. Maximum of 200 entries, no more than 150 entries recommended.
The id of the group it belongs to. Commands that do not match any group appear in the "Other" group at the end, and readData is listed in ungrouped.

The command line is displayed as is in a fixed-width font. Program names such as showai, ./showai, npm, node, etc. at the beginning are diluted; the first word after them is the command name and is bolded, which can be a CLI subcommand or MCP tool name (such as page_read, showai_capabilities, including _ . -); consecutive lowercase words (such as pages read) after the CLI subcommand are bolded, and the tool name is no longer bolded. Those starting with - are parameters, and uppercase words (PAGE, PATH) are considered placeholders.
One sentence purpose, displayed below the command and involved in the search. Plain text.
The expanded description supports **bold**,`代码`, [link](href); blank lines are segmented, and lines starting with "-" become a list. Do not participate in the search.
Parameter table, displayed in order, participates in search.

omission.description: The parameter table is not displayed. When detail, flags, and example are all omitted, the line cannot be expanded.

inputs.meaning: Parameter writing method, such as --home PATH. Should be unique within the same command.
Ready-to-run examples, displayed as is in the code panel with a copy button; can be multiple lines.

omission.description: The sample panel is not displayed.

inputs.meaning: Placeholder text for the search box.

omission.description: Displays "Search for command, parameter or purpose".
omission.value: Search for a command, parameter or purpose

recipes.title: Put together a CLI reference
steps: Divide into 3–7 groups by reader tasks (e.g. Run and Connect, Projects and Pages, Display and Export), not by source code module.
command writes the form in the help output (uppercase placeholders, square brackets indicate optional); summary writes what the reader uses it to do.
For commonly used commands, add flags and an example that can be run directly; for unpopular commands, just write a summary.
Use readData to check that ungrouped is empty and the number of each group is reasonable.

interactions.effect: Filter commands and highlight matches; the numbers on the group buttons update. Esc clears, ↓ moves to the first command.
Show only this group; click again to return to all.

interactions.action: Click the command line or press Enter
interactions.effect: Expand or collapse descriptions, parameters, and examples; ↑ ↓ moves between commands.
Copy the example; the sandbox prohibits copying when selecting code and prompting you to press ⌘C / Ctrl+C.

constraints: Reading operations do not modify page data.
The search is not case-sensitive and matches commands, purposes, and parameters by substring; detail and example do not participate in the search.
The list has no internal scrolling and grows in height with the displayed command; commands often rely on grouping and searching to shorten the list.

data: Commands[].group is updated synchronously when adding or deleting groups.
When the command writing method changes, the example is updated at the same time.
implementation: A new version is required for detail to participate in searches or to support command aliases.

entryPoints.purpose: Components, search index prepare(), matching and highlighting ranges() / marked(), command coloring CommandLine, CodePanel, md() / mdBlock() and readData.
Design tokens (including dark colors), search boxes, group buttons, lists, expanded details, parameter tables, code panels, empty states and narrow screen rules.

architecture: prepare() pre-calculates the lowercase command, purpose and parameter text for each command; only substring comparison is performed for each input, and no anti-shaking is required for more than 100 inputs. Search terms are deferred filtered through useDeferredValue and input remains smooth.

Highlighting calculates the matching interval on the entire command text, and then segments and renders it by word unit, so keywords that span subcommands and parameters (such as "pages read") can also be fully highlighted.
The expanded state is saved in a local Set keyed by the command index, and searches and filters are not reset.
extensionPoints: Classification rules for command tokens are in the CommandLine; suggestions for empty states are at the end of the component.
invariants: The component does not call onChange; all interactions only change local state.
Do not use dangerouslySetInnerHTML; both highlighting and inline markup generate React elements.
verification: Example 0: 5 groups of 40 items; search for theme and only pages read is left and list the matching parameters --theme dark in the line; search for "pages read" and highlight two words.
Searching for words that do not exist displays an empty state; when searching for other groups in a certain group, "View in all groups" is provided.
Check out the search box, grouping, expanded parameter table and code panel in 1000 px, 390 px and dark themes.
